# reversedock_service (Resource)

A ReverseDock service owned by the admin API (`name@api` in the running configuration), managed through `PUT` and `DELETE /api/v1/services/{name}`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "reversedock_service" "shop" {
  name = "shop"
  spec = jsonencode({
    backends = [
      { address = "10.0.0.5:8080" },
      { address = "10.0.0.6:8080" },
    ]
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the object, without a provider suffix: it starts with a letter or digit and uses letters, digits, `-`, `_` or `.` (at most 63 characters). References between API objects use the bare name. Changing it replaces the object.
- `spec` (String) The service as a JSON object, in the shape of the `services` section of the configuration file (see the configuration reference or `schema/rdock.v1.json`). Use `jsonencode(…)`. Formatting and key order never show as a change. The admin API fills in defaults and masks secrets it is shown (`***`); the provider keeps what you wrote unless the object really changed on the server. Write secrets as `${file:…}` or `${env:…}` references: the spec is stored in Terraform state as written.

### Read-Only

- `etag` (String) The `ETag` of the API's objects (all of them: they are one versioned document) as of the last time this resource was written or imported. Informational: every write sends the current ETag in `If-Match` itself.
- `id` (String) The name of the object.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the bare name of an API-owned object (not `shop@api`).
terraform import reversedock_service.shop shop
```
